name: Project Context navigation and the run trace's project-context block
description: Covers SPEC-01's two browser-only claims, ONE OF THEM VIA ITS DOCUMENTED FALLBACK. AC-57 (and the route half of AC-58): the sidebar's Project Context entry lands on the active repository's /repos/:repoId/context route. FALLBACK TAKEN (a): the `g x` chord is NOT driven here. `agent-browser` 0.35.1 does expose a key primitive (`press <key>`, retiring the plan's OQ-C), and the chord itself was verified by hand to fire and land on /repos/<id>/context — but `press` holds the key down, so one invocation dispatches ~180 auto-repeat keydowns and `press g` + `press x` produced ~90 interleaved chord activations, i.e. ~90 duplicate router.push calls that hammered the dev server and left the URL still settling past the 25s step timeout. There is no repeat-count flag on `press`. So the flow asserts the sidebar row instead, exactly as the plan's named fallback permits; AC-58's primary and guaranteed proof stays `client/src/components/app-shell/hooks/useGlobalShortcuts.test.ts`, which dispatches the two keydowns in jsdom and asserts router.push. AC-54 is driven through the block's OWN expand control (`find text ... click` on a role-less div — the plan's first-choice route, NOT its fallback), which is the strict reading of the criterion; `TraceBody.test.tsx` covers the same control hermetically. The Project Context page deliberately asserts the CLONING state, not a document list: the demo repo has clone_path: null (D-Q6g), so AC-1/AC-8/AC-11 have no seeded route and that is an accepted gap, not a bug. The phrase waited on ('Every public endpoint must document its rate limit') is SEED_CONTEXT_PHRASE in server/src/db/seed-context.ts — change that seed and change this flow with it. Read-only: it opens and clicks; it attaches nothing and triggers no model call.
